purpose: Writing patterns for synthetic demo drafts; source reviewers are not identities for generated content.
authenticity: Publicly published reviews; authorship and purchase authenticity not independently verified.
method: Deduplicated review-body features from public Judge.me markup; heuristic English filtering. No full review bodies or customer names retained.

profiles.guidance: Start directly with one visible color or pattern detail, then give a brief personal reaction. One sentence is enough.
Give one understated personal opinion about what is visible. Use everyday words and stop after the point.
Use two uneven sentences: a specific shirt detail, then how it looks with the bottoms actually visible. Do not invent an occasion.
A short conversational fragment about a visible detail is fine. Avoid an advertising headline or a generic compliment.
Begin with a restrained personal reaction, then explain it using one detail actually visible in the image. Do not start with I love.
Point out a visible detail in plain language, then add a short reaction. Let the second sentence be shorter than the first.
Write one complete sentence about the strongest visible detail. No list of benefits or extra closing endorsement.
Use a relaxed first-person observation and a second sentence about a different visible detail. Natural contractions are fine; avoid polished sales copy.
